title: Global patterns of ecologically unequal exchange: Implications for sustainability in the 21st century
status: Toolkit R reconstruction executed; approximate fit agreement; exact reproduction unresolved

levels.mechanism: Investigates ecologically unequal exchange through asymmetries in embodied resource and labour flows between countries.
levels.strategy: Accounts for embodied materials, energy, land and labour in trade and examines relationships with income and other factors.
levels.technique: Eora multiregional input–output accounting, trade in value added and piecewise structural equation modelling.
levels.output: Embodied material, energy, land and labour flows; trade in value added and modelled statistical relationships.

title: Imperialist appropriation in the world economy: Drain from the global South through unequal exchange, 1990–2015
summary: Examines resource appropriation through unequal exchange in the world economy over 1990–2015.
status: Methodological profile under development; replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Interprets net North–South appropriation of embodied resources and labour through unequal exchange.
levels.strategy: Reaggregates embodied-flow estimates into North–South net transfers and adds monetary valuation calculations.
levels.technique: Uses the Eora v.199.82 MRIO dataset reported by Dorninger et al. (2021), covering 1990–2015; adds monetary calculations.
levels.output: Net embodied transfers of materials, energy, land and labour, alongside monetary estimates.

title: How much growth is required to achieve good lives for all? Insights from needs-based analysis
summary: Synthesises needs-based poverty research and compares published decent-living energy and material requirements with current global resource use. It is not an unequal-exchange flow estimate.
status: Source-based methodological profile; independent replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Examines how meeting basic needs and providing decent living standards relate to economic growth and resource requirements; does not estimate an unequal-exchange mechanism.
levels.strategy: Synthesises needs-based thresholds and published decent-living resource estimates and compares these with current resource use.
levels.technique: Literature-based synthesis and scenario comparison; adjusts IEA energy figures using a territorial-to-consumption-based ratio reported in Hickel et al. (2022). No full MRIO rerun.
levels.output: Needs-based income thresholds and comparisons of energy and material requirements with current resource use; not an estimate of unequal-exchange flows.

title: A Note on the Concept of Delinking
summary: Develops the concept of delinking through an illustrative comparison of national-popular and world-capitalist development strategies.
status: Source-based methodological profile in preparation; illustrative model not independently reproduced

levels.mechanism: Delinking reorganises development priorities around a nationally grounded and popular law of value rather than subordinating them to the world-capitalist law of value.
levels.strategy: Compares two illustrative development strategies for an initially identical economy over ten years, using shared assumptions about population growth, productivity and investment.
levels.technique: Illustrative comparative modelling of sectoral production, relative prices, income distribution and growth. Detailed technical derivations are referred to Amin (1982).
levels.output: Contrasting illustrative growth and distribution outcomes under national-popular and world-capitalist development strategies; not independently reproduced empirical estimates.

title: The Law of World Value
summary: Investigates persistent international monetary inequality and proposes a pluralist research programme to explain divergence; presents the Monetary Inequality Index (MII).
status: Methodological profile updated from author-shared manuscript; author review invited; independent reproduction not undertaken

levels.mechanism: Proposes that persistent world-market price–value differences generate unequal realisation advantages, reinforcing technological rents, investment capacity and structural divergence.
levels.strategy: Compares historically specified country blocs; distinguishes monetary, consumption and productive inequality; contrasts employment-based productive contributions with monetary value realised.
levels.technique: Monetary Inequality Index (MII), Theil decomposition, Employee Inequality Index (EII), labour-based produced-versus-realised value comparisons and world MELT.
levels.output: Monetary divergence series, bloc comparisons and reported labour-based estimates of realisation gains and losses. The MII alone does not establish causation.

title: Unequal Exchange: A Study of the Imperialism of Trade
category: Prices of production and international wages
summary: Develops a theory of unequal exchange through international wage differences and price formation, with implications for international distribution.
status: Source-based conceptual profile using bibliographic record and Emmanuel’s openly accessible 1975 elaboration; 1972 book not fully checked; no independent reproduction

levels.mechanism: International wage differentials, in the context of mobile capital and tendencies toward profit-rate equalisation, affect international prices of production and distribution.
levels.strategy: Develops theoretical arguments and comparative price systems; the 1975 elaboration sets out algebraic and numerical examples and a modified Sraffa framework.
levels.technique: Theoretical price-of-production equations and comparative examples. This is not an observed international value-transfer time series.
levels.output: A theoretical account of international unequal exchange and its distributive implications, rather than a independently replicated monetary estimate.

title: The Structure of Global Money and World Tables of Unequal Exchange
summary: Investigates the non-homogeneous international value of money and uses international price/exchange-rate comparisons to estimate unequal exchange.
status: Source-based preliminary profile; article metadata and abstract verified; precise tables and calculation steps require full-text checking; replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Proposes that systematic currency undervaluation and international exchange-rate structures contribute to transfers between low- and high-income countries.
levels.strategy: Relates purchasing-power comparisons to market exchange-rate valuation and applies an exchange-rate distortion approach to international exchange.
levels.technique: International price-level or PPP versus market-exchange-rate comparison, with trade data used in unequal-exchange estimation; exact implementation to be documented from full text.
levels.output: Published world tables and estimated unequal-exchange quantities, whose numerical results have not been independently checked here.

title: The Wealth of (Some) Nations: Imperialism and the Mechanics of Value Transfer
summary: Examines mechanisms of imperial value transfer, including unequal exchange of embodied labour, and their implications for international class relations.
status: Source-based preliminary profile informed by accessible book text; chapter-level numerical procedures and sources not independently audited; replication not attempted

levels.mechanism: Connects international value transfer, wage differentiation and imperial relations to the reproduction of class and consumption hierarchies.
levels.strategy: Combines historical and theoretical political economy with quantitative discussion of labour embodied in international exchange.
levels.technique: Comparison of labour embodied in imports and exports alongside analysis of price, wage and monopoly relations; individual numerical estimates require source-by-source verification.
levels.output: Historical and theoretical claims and quantitative illustrations concerning international value transfer; not independently replicated.
